items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: He told me that he was working at the Cafe Society Uptown with Billy Moore and a pianist.

ctx.x: Jack Crystal who worked in Milt's record shop was in charge of the session which featured many well known black and white musicians: Art Hodes, Pee Wee Russell, Bobby Hackett, George Wettling, Rod Cless, Sid Catlett, Hank Duncan, Sandy Williams, Wild Bill Davison and Oran "Hot Lips" Page to name a few that participated in these sessions which really jumped. There were always two bottles of whisky furnished by Milt to get the sessions in a swinging mood. The closing number was always 'Bugle Call Rag' and I'm…

One day, Al Hall came to my house and asked me if I would like to replace a guitarist named Billy Moore who was sick in a hospital. My brother(who was a tailor) and I were sharing a three-roomed furnished apartment on 161st Street and I had not seen Al for quite some time. He told me that he was working at the Cafe Society Uptown with Billy Moore and a pianist.

I was surprised because Teddy Wilson had told me two years before that Barney Josephson had said that he never wanted Al and myself in his place again. I accepted to replace Billy until he came out of the hospital and that night I met the pianist. His name was Ellis Larkins, was from Baltimore and had been studying at Julliard music college on a scholarship he had won in his home town.
